text:
I can't really say how likely she is to get denied entry at the border, except to say that travelling here again so soon after an almost 3-month visit is going to be a red flag and I wouldn't be surprised if there are at least some problems/questions. How long is she planning to visit for? 

In circumstances like this, even if they do let her in, it's not uncommon for them to give a shorter permit (e.g. just a couple of weeks). To be safe, I would recommend that she plan to keep this visit quite short, have a return ticket, and bring copies of the wedding invitations to show the border official (even just on her phone). It might seem overkill, but it wouldn't hurt for her to have a letter from her employer in English confirming that she works there and explaining when she will return to work. Maybe even a letter from you would be helpful (with your TZ and phone number) explaining she'll be staying with you, and when she plans to leave. You should also have your phone on you when she lands in case border officials want to call you :) 

If she is denied entry, it usually means she will no longer be able to rely on the visa-waiver agreement between Israel and Switzerland for future visits.  So if she wants to come visit Israel again, she would need to either apply for a tourist visa at the embassy in Switzerland, or you will need to submit an invitation at your local PIBA office. It's not the end of the world, but it is annoying. However, I don't see it having an impact on any future partner visa application.
